record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let M be an equivariant map algebra M(X,g)^Γ, formed from an affine scheme X, a target algebra g, and a compatible Γ-action. Develop representation-theoretic categories beyond finite-dimensional M-modules, including analogues of category O, categories of integrable highest-weight representations, categories of quasifinite representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces, and other suitable infinite-dimensional module categories.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(c) Possibly infinite-dimensional representations. Much of the current focus in the study of the representation theory of arbitrary EMAs has been on the category of finite-dimensional representations. However, in specific cases (most importantly, the loop and current algebras) more general categories of representations have been studied.

It would be interesting to study analogous categories in the more arbitrary EMA setting. For example, one could consider the category of integrable highest weight rep- resentations, the category of quasifinite representations (i.e. representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces) or appropriate generalizations of category O.

artifact.status_search_result: The general program of developing infinite-dimensional representation categories for arbitrary equivariant map algebras remains open as a broad research direction. Substantial partial progress has been made for specific families: integrable representations of equivariant map algebras associated with Borel-de Siebenthal pairs, global/local Weyl modules, quasifinite modules for map Virasoro and map Witt algebras, and integrable representations of root-graded Lie algebras. A complete theory (category O analogues, quasifinite classification) for arbitrary EMAs has not been established.
